description.en-US: The contact this profile makes a vendor. One row per party per organization, which is what the unique index enforces — a second row would give one supplier two sets of payment terms with no way to say which applies. Immutable: moving a profile to a different party would silently reassign every purchase order that named the first.

How far the vendor has got through qualification. It is an ordinary field rather than a state machine in this phase: no transition here has side effects, so there is nothing for a domain action to protect. Only 'active' should be orderable from, and Purchase enforces that at order confirmation rather than the schema, because the rule belongs to Purchase.
Why the vendor is suspended or blacklisted. Free text, because the reasons are not enumerable in advance and a wrong enum value is worse than a sentence someone can read.

The currency this vendor normally invoices in, used to default a purchase order's currency. A plain id with no edge: the currency belongs to Essential, and a foreign key across a module boundary would make Contacts' schema depend on Essential's table. Validated by a port call instead.

The agreed terms, as text — 'Net 30', '50% deposit'. Deliberately not a structured due-date rule: there is no payment-terms master anywhere in the system yet, and inventing a half-model here would have to be migrated when a real one arrives.

How many days this vendor usually takes to deliver, used to default a purchase order's expected arrival. Capped at ten years, which is not a business rule so much as a guard against a typo becoming a delivery date centuries away.
